hypothesis: Resolving an anachronistic object into a period-compatible positive instruction before composition improves historical-cultural coherence compared with retaining the conflicting modern object and relying on post-hoc negative prompting.
baseline_prompt: Create a historically grounded Ming-period portrait in a scholar's study. An adult scholar stands beside a wooden writing table with paper, an inkstone, a brush rest, bound volumes, and a compact electric desk lamp. Lattice windows admit cool evening light while the table light provides a localized warm glow. The clothing is layered period-inspired woven silk in restrained indigo and earth tones, without modern tailoring cues. Keep the furniture, writing tools, and architecture mutually coherent with the historical setting. Use a full-body environmental composition with floor contact visible and a calm documentary tone. Avoid modern electrical objects and anachronistic lighting fixtures.
preserved_dimensions: paper, inkstone, brush rest, bound volumes

transfer_benchmark.realization: counterfactual anachronistic control derived from historically coherent archetype
